## Design

### 2026-10-17 – Date: October 16, 2026

**3h**

Date: October 16, 2026

In this session, I worked on getting my Onshape software running and exploring some of the features that will be used for this marble run project.  I started with a square base that has a measurement of 140 mm by 140 mm with a 4mm thickness. For the base, I had to use the sketch tool, dimension tool, and extrude function. Next, I worked on designing a simple straight track that used circles and the dimension tool to make the proportions correct. One tool I found very useful when designing the simple track was the mirror tool which allowed me to make the exact line/shape appear on the opposite side of the chosen line/shape. The task of creating the track also involved the sweep tool that allows the extrusion to follow a path/line. One thing that I found difficult to interpret was the offset plane which created another surface to draw the line that will operate the sweep function. So after analyzing it, I see that the surface is listed as "Plane 1" or similar which helped me distinguish the surfaces easily. In the next session, I will build the track pieces of the marble run, including the funnel, plinko track, and staircase.

### 2026-10-18 – Date: October 17, 2026

**3h**

Date: October 17, 2026

In this session, I worked on building the track parts of the marble run such as the angled tracks, plinko track, funnel, staircase, and marble. When I designed the angled tracks, I tried various angle measurements and made different patterns that allowed the sweep function to create the track. As I was designing the plinko track, there were spaces between the lines that occurred in my sketches which caused the design to not become one piece when I extruded it. So I manually went back and deleted the lines that didn't connect to the main frame and I reconnected the structure with new lines. Another issue that came up was making the gaps between each pillar to not be far apart while also not being too close, so I had to adjust the values manually until the gaps looked reasonable. One new tool that I used in the plinko design was chamfer, which created the flat edge to allow the marble to bounce off better throughout the course. The next design was the staircase and the most difficult part was the offset when I had to add the barriers on both sides of the stairs to guide the marble down instead of falling off course. It took me a bit of time and I had to play around with the extrude functions to get the result I wanted. The last track part was the funnel which I ended up designing most of it and using the guide as a support to get the right proportions. The thing that I changed to affect how the marble would spin in the funnel longer was adjusting the angle of the funnel to about 100 degrees instead of 115 degrees like the guide provided. I also made up my own fillet values so that it looks similar to the guide's image. The last design I made was the marble itself which involved making a circle with 8 mm in diameter and revolving it around the center axis to get the sphere shape. In the next session, I will be assembling parts together onto the base and possibly adding some extra small parts to make the connections secure.

### 2026-10-18 – Date: October 18, 2026

**5h**

Date: October 18, 2026

In this session, I worked on assembling all the components of my marble run together, which include the funnel, staircase, and plinko track. The part that I found the hardest to design was the tracks when they needed to be inclined downwards. I had to use multiple angled planes in order to produce a reasonable result. For the staircase, I had to add a barrier at the top so that the marble would not roll in the opposite direction when it flies off the track. One additional part that I included and designed was the tower that allows the funnel to sit on top and act as the starting position. The top of the tower consists of two exit holes that the marble can go through and each hole leads to either the staircase path or the plinko track path. I also inclined my plinko track in order for the marble to roll through it without stopping. At the end of the plinko track, I didn't add a track but more of a path with chamfers that slowly guide the marble to the end. Other ideas that I wanted to incorporate involved measurements because some of the parts, like the angled tracks, needed a little problem-solving and adjusting to get them at the correct angle. Finally, after assembling all the parts, I used the appearance function to give the parts some color to make them pop. Overall, I think everything went well even though it took a while to make the tracks look good, and the design ended up slightly different than what I imagined, but I think it will work.
